recap.text: Colonel Boomer is a level 62 elven Legate and commander of the 106th Bloody Leeches who smells of cedar and acorns. He leads the southern assault, fighting Reaver paratroopers and planning a move on the Operatic castle. After the dungeon, he offers a poem to York and sets aside four Cronus suits and a skiff for a pregnant veteran.

beats.headline: A pickled bulldog with elf ears
beats.text: Subject: Boomer. Elven Legate. Level 62. Colonel in the Princess Posse, commanding the 106th Bloody Leeches. A grizzled elf who survived one of the earliest seasons, bowed out on the tenth floor, and lived as a merchant on the sixth for many seasons before escaping. Crawler Carl's description is a bulldog pickled for five thousand years with elf ears and a cigar. Banned from CrawlCon for threatening an orcish showrunner during a panel. Wanted for a killing in a waystation brawl that started as an argument about the crawl. Crawler Donut reports he smells of cedar and acorns.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer is a level 62 elven legate and commander of the 106th Bloody Leeches.

beats.headline: Cheese sticks and Monkeywrenchers
beats.text: The briefing, conducted with an unlit cigar. The Dream's bombardiers are cowards who run if you get near their chuckers. The cavalry is the thing to watch, and so is Epitome Tagg's household guard. Of the robed Madness troops going invisible, probably few are real Viceroys, but the invisible ones are Monkeywrenchers, and twenty of them once took two castles in the first hours. His boys and girls have had breakfast. Then Crawler Carl says let's do this, and Boomer lights the cigar, takes one very long puff, and fills the bunker with smoke. Fuck yeah, he says.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer briefs Carl with an unlit cigar about cowards, cavalry, and invisible Monkeywrenchers.

beats.headline: Command of the assault
beats.text: Warlord menu: command of the southern assault transferred to Colonel Boomer. His first order is to stop celebrating. Nobody fights harder than someone trapped, he tells the generals. Form up, do not push too hard, and let them think it is a stalemate rather than a surrender. They have maybe half an hour before the enemy either escapes or has to be killed. Then the generals get on with it, and Crawler Carl turns north to meet Party Planner.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer takes command of the southern assault and orders the generals to stop celebrating.

beats.headline: Salty about the naga castle
beats.text: The southern trenches are filled with scrolls and the enemy artillery wrecked, and Boomer is sore about not pushing on to take the naga castle. Crawler Carl concedes privately that it would have been the safest and smartest play, and does not care. Boomer pulls most of the 106th north to help Florin. Then, on the band: a group of flyers that are not the Posse's have just buzzed him, moving low and fast toward the castle. They are Reaver paratroopers, and they arrive.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer moves the 106th north to help Florin while Reaver paratroopers buzz him.

beats.headline: Time to move on the castle
beats.text: Walking back to the castle through un-looted Reaver paratrooper corpses, Boomer gives Crawler Carl the debrief. The map is a mess. The 104th is back on castle defence, but most of the mages were lost to the brain worm attack, and the magical defences are going to take a while. The good news is that the enemy is more fractured than the Posse. Now might be a time, he says, to move on the Operatic castle. That, too, is code, and Carl agrees it is time.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer debriefs Carl among un-looted Reaver paratrooper corpses and suggests moving on the Operatic castle.

beats.headline: The Reavers are Boomer's operation
beats.text: The Reaver assault is Boomer's. When Crawler Carl wants to pull General Louis off a bomb run because of the dragon circling the castle, Boomer tells him no, over the private band. They have no No Disassemble missiles, the ground troops need that air support, and Carl handed operational command to Rosetta after putting Boomer in charge of this assault. Focus on your own operation, not mine. Carl belays his order and tells Louis this is Boomer's op, and to listen to him. Then Sledge reports missiles incoming on the Reaver castle.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer runs the Reaver assault.

beats.headline: Roses are red
beats.text: Out of the dungeon now, aged, on a low-resolution screen aboard the Homecoming Queen. He asks York whether he has written any new poems, as he always does, and offers one of his own in the style of an Earth classic: roses are red, violets are blue, we won Faction Wars, now we get to kill more of them. York calls it a terrible poem. Boomer asks after the breaching suits, sets aside four Cronus suits and a skiff for a pregnant veteran on the surface, and says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon. Better warm up the lasers.
beats.gist: Colonel Boomer asks York for poems and offers one about killing after winning Faction Wars.

relations.note: Publicly disowned, privately in close contact
